## Problem

Found while running echo-loop experiments for bug `00c1-dc03-1f1f-4ffc` (anarchic-princely-raven). This is a **test-harness** defect, not a production one, but it silently produces a WRONG-LOOKING production behaviour in any test that exercises keyless-pending binding recovery.

`binding_recovery.recover_pending_bindings` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_recovery.py:343-350`) falls back to the LEGACY hyphen JQL form `labels = "rebar-id-<local_id>"` when the modern colon form `labels = "rebar-id:<local_id>"` returns no hit.

The stateful Jira fake `_FakeClient.search_issues` in `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py` (~line 76-93) special-cases ONLY the colon prefix. The hyphen query therefore falls through to its window-search branch and returns **every open issue**. `recover_pending_bindings` then `bind_confirm`s `results[0]["key"]`, binding the pending local ticket to an arbitrary unrelated issue — after which the outbound differ emits an UPDATE against that issue carrying a DIFFERENT ticket's summary, priority and status.

Real Jira JQL label-equality cannot return an unlabelled issue, so this cannot happen in production. It is purely an artifact of the fake being incomplete. But it makes the fake unfaithful in exactly the area the fake exists to model, and any future test touching keyless-pending recovery will get a confidently wrong result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_FakeClient.search_issues` recognises BOTH identity-label JQL forms — `labels = "rebar-id:<id>"` and the legacy `labels = "rebar-id-<id>"` — and answers each as a label-equality search (empty when no issue carries that label), never as a window search.
- [ ] A regression test drives `recover_pending_bindings` against the fake with a pending local whose issue carries NO identity label, and asserts NO binding is created (rather than a binding to an unrelated key).
- [ ] The existing tests in `test_reconcile_idempotency.py` still pass unchanged.

## Evidence

Reproduced in `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_echo_loop_experiment.py` (perturbation (e), lagging-index client), which models both JQL forms explicitly and therefore does NOT hit the artifact — the contrast is what exposed it.
compiled_state.title: Reconciler integration fake answers the legacy hyphen rebar-id JQL as a window search, letting recover_pending_bindings mis-bind to an unrelated issue
